facts.text: Hunts Point takes its name from Thomas Hunt, an English settler who owned the peninsula in the late 1660s.
The peninsula sits where the Bronx River meets the East River, forming a tidal strait that links Upper New York Bay to Long Island Sound.
In the 1970s and 1980s, residents and groups like The Point Community Development Corporation fought redlining, fires, and abandonment to reclaim the waterfront.
The Point, housed in a former bagel factory, now hosts performance art, galleries, and after‑school programs that nurture local talent.
Sustainable South Bronx, founded by Majora Carter, secured funding to build two waterfront parks, giving the neighborhood its first formal river access in sixty years.
Jazz legends once played at the Hunts Point Palace, a club that made the neighborhood a hotspot for music during the mid‑20th century.
